reviewer: Codex, independent; did not author this candidate
protocol: Independent adversarial review; refute not confirm; other current reviewer not read
reviewScope: Review only. This review does not mark DR-112 SATISFIED, does not qualify or demonstrate anything, does not authorize implementation, and does not apply or seal the candidate.
summary: The source carries, role separation, monotonic-store join, no-network posture, numeric reservations, DR-110/DR-113 deferrals, and DR-103 byte-level ownership boundary are sound. The candidate nevertheless fails its central claim to provide a reviewable state machine. The transition relation is partial and nondeterministic; transitions into TRUSTED omit the DR-112 envelope/delegation/threshold half of the accepted DR-103 split and do not enforce the state's own freshness invariant; and the offline-running policy is not total and contains overlapping contradictory cases. Two additional source/audit defects require repair. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. DR-112 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes no implementation.

blockers.title: The declared transition relation is partial and nondeterministic
blockers.measurement: The artifact declares 7 states and 8 events, hence 56 state/event pairs. Expanding the two wildcard rows covers only 24 pairs; 32 have no transition and there is no general default-refuse/default-no-op rule. EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD has no path from EXPIRED, STALE-REVOCATION, QUORUM-LOST, REVOKED, or RECOVERY, so ordinary signed refresh cannot recover expiry or stale revocation and a presented recovery payload has no defined presentation transition from the very states that need recovery. EV-REVOKE and EV-QUORUM-OBSERVE exist only from TRUSTED, so a later accepted revocation or quorum observation has no state effect after expiry/staleness. EV-RECOVER-COMMIT has no explicit refusal outside RECOVERY and recovery has no abort/failure path. The wildcard EV-INSTALL target 'same or refuse' is not a state or a deterministic outcome. FC-RECOVER says ST-* -> ST-RECOVERY although EV-RECOVER-BEGIN accepts only four of the seven states.
blockers.nondeterminism: From TRUSTED, one EV-CLOCK observation can simultaneously satisfy 'time at or after metadataExpiry' and 'last-known revocation older than freshness floor', enabling two different target states with no priority. Expiry, staleness, quorum loss, and revocation can coexist, but the flat state set has no composite representation or precedence. Event order therefore controls the visible state: after CLOCK moves a role to EXPIRED or STALE-REVOCATION, a newer byte-valid EV-REVOKE has no transition to REVOKED. This is incompatible with the promised monotonic revocation observation and can hide the safety-dominant condition.
blockers.whyBlocker: The live DR-112 acceptance cell specifically requires a reviewed state machine. A partial relation with overlapping guards and no refusal semantics cannot be reviewed as a deterministic safety machine, and the missing refresh path leaves the row's named refresh behavior undefined.
blockers.minimumRepair: Define a deterministic and total event relation: either explicit behavior for every pair or a stated default refusal/no-op with an auditable outcome; represent simultaneous conditions as independent flags/composite states or declare a safety precedence; add ordinary refresh paths from expired/stale states; process revocation and quorum observations from every relevant state; define recovery failure/abort and invalid-commit refusal; use real state targets plus typed outcomes; and add event-order/combined-condition fixtures. Preserve the DR-110 and DR-113 deferrals.

blockers.title: TRUSTED entry omits DR-112's half of the signature-validity split
blockers.governingBoundary: The accepted component-manifest-schemas.v2 RJ-4 makes only UNSIGNED and DIGEST_MISMATCH active. ENVELOPE_MISMATCH remains inactive pending the canonical-JSON surface and DR-112 envelope/key semantics. Its ID-DEP-5 assigns signature-envelope validity, delegated publisher/component namespaces, expiry/revocation/rotation/quorum/recovery metadata to DR-112, and TC-SIG explicitly routes wrong-key, expired-metadata, revoked-namespace, and threshold-failure fixtures to the DR-112 corpus.
blockers.measurement: UNBOOTSTRAPPED -> TRUSTED guards only on payload completeness, DR-103 byte-level verification, not expired, and not revoked. That does not establish an authorized root/key, delegated namespace, envelope preimage validity, signer threshold, last-known-revocation freshness, or future-issued-at bound. In particular, stale revocation is distinct from revoked, so a complete stale payload satisfies the written guard while violating ST-TRUSTED's own 'inside ... last-known-revocation floors' definition. The TRUSTED refresh guard says only 'newer consistent snapshot' and does not restate byte verification or any trust-policy checks. RECOVERY -> TRUSTED says 'new roots accepted' without defining who may accept them. Outside the verbatim source carry, delegated publisher/component namespace policy is absent; no fixture covers wrong key or revoked namespace.
blockers.consequence: On the literal guards, a payload with a present envelope and matching digests but an unauthorized/self-supplied root or wrong delegated namespace can pass the only invoked active DR-103 checks and enter TRUSTED. This does not re-own DR-103; it leaves the complementary DR-112 validity rule missing and creates a fail-open trust bootstrap.
blockers.whyBlocker: A state called TRUSTED cannot be entered before the artifact's own trust owner has established the signer, delegation, threshold, freshness, and future-time conditions. This is the safety boundary the accepted DR-103 contract deliberately reserved to DR-112.
blockers.minimumRepair: Define the parameterized, non-numeric trust-policy shape: bootstrap anchor custody; role-to-key and delegated namespace authority; envelope/preimage join; rotation and recovery authority; threshold evaluation against the reserved parameter; expiry, freshness, future-time, and anti-rollback checks. Require the complete predicate on every transition into or remaining in TRUSTED, with failed guards staying non-TRUSTED and refusing. Add wrong-key, revoked-namespace, threshold-failure, stale-bootstrap, future-bootstrap, and recovery-envelope fixtures. Leave quorum and clock values reserved.

blockers.title: The offline-running policy is neither total nor conflict-resolved
blockers.measurement: EV-CONTINUE applies in every state but delegates all behavior to four offlineRunningPolicy rows. There is no row or default for the all-TRUSTED baseline; INDEX REVOKED or QUORUM-LOST; COMPONENT EXPIRED, STALE-REVOCATION, QUORUM-LOST, or RECOVERY; CORE EXPIRED, STALE-REVOCATION, or RECOVERY; or mixtures of those states. Existing rows can conflict: INDEX EXPIRED + COMPONENT TRUSTED permits continuation without constraining CORE, while CORE REVOKED or QUORUM-LOST permits nothing. With both conditions true, the artifact gives both answers and no precedence. FC-CONTINUE exercises only the single expired-index/trusted-component case.
blockers.whyBlocker: Emergency/current-component continuation is in the DR-112 row itself and the carried source says currently verified components may continue only under the reviewed offline-running policy. A partial, overlapping rule list cannot determine whether a process may continue and can choose a permissive row while a safety-dominant role is revoked.
blockers.minimumRepair: Provide a total core/index/component continuation decision table or an explicit safety-ordered predicate with a fail-closed default. Distinguish already-running continuation from starting a new process, define precedence for combined role states, cover the trusted baseline and every non-TRUSTED condition, and add cross-product/precedence fixtures. Keep newly revoked replay deferred to DR-113 and repair-media outside scope.

shouldFix.title: Refusals fall outside the transition-only audit contract
shouldFix.detail: auditAndWaiver says every transition appends {role, from, to, event, payloadDigests, clockObservation}. Guard failures are written as 'stay ... and refuse' or are absent pairs, not transitions, so they produce no required audit entry. The record has no accepted/refused outcome or refusal reason. FC-AG-MISSING asks only for a run log. The live DR-G08 row's required retained evidence explicitly includes recovery and refusal audit.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make every attempted event, including guard failure and default refusal, emit an audit record with typed outcome/refusal reason and unchanged-state information; require refusal-audit assertions in the negative fixtures. Do not turn operational audit into sealed evidence.

shouldFix.title: Two candidate-only shorthand labels are presented as live DR-row vocabulary
shouldFix.detail: 'DR-107 P-8' is a label minted by lifecycle-generation-contract.v1, whose bytes are CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW / DO-NOT-SEAL / binds NOTHING; the live file-04 source contains the underlying eighth bullet but never the token P-8. Likewise SC-OPS is minted by state-class-contract.v1 with the same candidate-only standing and occurs nowhere in live file 08, files 03/04, or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. Neither candidate is recorded or candidate-marked here. The underlying propositions are supported: file 04 lines 78-79 state the monotonic-store separation, and live DR-124 names operational metadata. The defect is provenance, not substance.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Restate both joins in the pinned live-source vocabulary ('the file-04 monotonic trust-state bullet' and 'the live DR-124 operational-metadata class'), or add each candidate by exact path/digest and explicitly say citation does not accept it or its owning DR row.

attackResults.mintedQuorumClockWaiverNumbers: PASS. Threshold cardinality, clock skew/freshness, emergency permission, and waiver duration are named parameters with RESERVED/Not minted standing. No policy value or duration is selected.
attackResults.repairMediaShipping: PASS. TR-REPAIR and repair material are named, but shipping and use remain deferred with DR-110; FC-REPAIR-NAMED is explicitly non-executable for G08.
attackResults.newlyRevokedReplay: PASS. The replay case is named and deferred with DR-113 consistently with DR202-RR-F4; no replay continuation behavior is designed.
attackResults.dr103ByteLevelOwnership: PASS on ownership. RJ-4 UNSIGNED/DIGEST_MISMATCH remain with the accepted DR-103 contract and this artifact claims ceremony semantics only. SITCV1-B2 is the converse defect: the DR-112 half is absent, not that DR-103's half is seized.
attackResults.implicitNetworkOrFailOpenRefresh: PASS for network behavior. There is no network event; payload presentation is air-gap/removable-media; missing input explicitly forbids download, refresh, and lock mutation. The fail-open trust-bootstrap defect is separately graded at SITCV1-B2.
attackResults.roleCollapse: PASS. Five trust roles are named and machine.discipline requires one machine per role; core expiry is expressly not index expiry.
attackResults.trustCounterRollback: PASS. Trust roots, revocation observations, expiry floors, and anti-rollback counters are separate from executable generation pointers, and recovery cannot move them backward.
attackResults.satisfiedQualifiedOrImplementationAuthor: PASS. Header standing is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW / DO-NOT-SEAL / binds NOTHING. SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, execution, and implementation references are negative. DR-112 remains OPEN.
attackResults.rowVerbatim: PASS. Exactly one live line begins '| DR-112 |', at line 294, and it is byte-identical to rowVerbatim including OPEN / Hard blocker.
attackResults.sourceAndCarryIntegrity: PASS. All 5 recorded governing-source digests reproduce. File 03 lines 76-89 and file 04 lines 212-224 match the carried arrays exactly, 14/14 and 13/13 lines. The subject parses with zero duplicate JSON keys.
